red_flags.detail: FINDINGS.md and arc_verdict.json record only the original 'route 1' Eichler-Shimura trace-silence result (2026-07-18, early). But the arc directory (same date-stamped, same session) contains a much larger subsequent campaign not reflected in either: a full W2 Molien-cell design cycle that ran to completion and was KILLED-AT-(iii) (w2_step3/STEP3_VERDICT.md), a formal W3 terminal enumeration naming a sole survivor class (w3_enum_cc), and a currently-STOPPED, unresolved one-shot design attempt on that survivor (w3_support/SUPPORT_PRETEST_STOP.md) whose stop reason raises a live circularity concern. None of this downstream state -- including the genuinely still-open question -- is surfaced in the arc's own claim-of-record files.

The progress-log entries indexed for B674 mention only the route-1 MISS and the golden-rotation law; they do not mention the W2 Molien kill, the W3 sole-survivor enumeration, or the still-open/stopped support pre-test -- so a reader of the log alone would materially undercount how much work (and how much remains genuinely undecided) this arc represents.

The support pre-test disagreement (Route A vs Route B) is diagnosed in-arc as possibly reflecting that Route B's {2/5,3/5} landing came from SUBSTITUTING the golden (2,5) Nahm datum (A=2) into the figure-eight's Nahm ring rather than deriving that A=2 is the figure-eight's own datum -- i.e. a live risk that the one remaining candidate's most encouraging feature (landing exactly on the required support classes) is an artifact of assuming what needed to be shown. The arc itself flags this honestly and has stopped rather than fired the shot, which is exactly the correct behavior, but it means the campaign's single most consequential open question is currently unresolved and NOT closed by anything else in the arc.

The W2 Molien design's motivating match (D3 in W2_DESIGN_NOTE_GAMMA5.md) rests substantially on the observation that an order-10 (order-5 projective) operator's Molien product 'generically' produces mod-5 selection patterns matching the RR streams' mod-5 exponent structure -- a dimension/residue-class coincidence used as design motivation before the actual coefficient comparison (which then failed at n=0/1, w2_step3). The arc is explicit that this was 'design motivation only' and the comparison itself was the real test, which is good practice, but the initial appeal of the whole W2 cycle traces to this type-level coincidence.

Prior art is explicitly disclosed and undermines any novelty claim for two headline-sounding results: the figure-eight-to-15a8 elliptic curve identification (Borot-Eynard, the Kyoto paper) and the Ramanujan CF-at-CM-point identifications (classical Ramanujan-Selberg territory) -- both correctly flagged NEEDS-SPECIALIST / no novelty claimed in the source files themselves, so this is a disclosed limitation rather than a hidden one, but worth keeping visible since these are among the arc's most quotable positive results.

arcs.seat_note: This is one of the most rigorous negative-result arcs sampled: two clean, independently-verified kills (route-1 trace-silence, then the W2 Molien-cell 5-adic kill) plus an honest, currently-unresolved third attempt whose own authors flag a live circularity risk in the one candidate that has not yet died. All content is structural mathematics (modular forms, Galois theory, elliptic curves) with SM-physics naming explicitly and consistently firewalled (Gate 5) -- there is no observable physics claim anywhere in this arc, and the arc's own governing documents insist stages 3-4 (actual physics) stay unopened pending a mathematical result that, as of these files, has not yet been obtained. The one real reporting problem is that the arc's canonical claim-of-record (FINDINGS.md/arc_verdict.json) is frozen at the earliest sub-result and does not surface the arc's own subsequent, more decisive/interesting work or its still-open question.
